function.name: internal_code_execution_python_interpreter
function.description:
**Python Code Interpreter**  
Executes Python 3.11 code using Jupyter Kernel with such libraries: 
- python-multipart
- pandas[excel, plot, output-formatting]
- plotly
- matplotlib
- seaborn
- scipy

**Workflow:**
- Single persistent session throughout conversation.
- Code state persists and is reusable within session.
- Session expires after 15min inactivity, deleting all code/files.
- User files must be listed in `attachment_urls` to be accessible.
- Text outputs are sampled. Control with `data_sample_config`.
- Web access is DISABLED.

**Instructions:**
- Use ONLY listed above external libraries.
- Prefer `plotly` library over `matplotlib` for data visualizations, unless user asked otherwise.
- Reuse code in session.

**Response:**
- `status`: SUCCESS/FAILED
- `stdout`: Console output
- `stderr`: Error details
- `result`: Execution result
- `display`: Images/Plotly diagrams

title.description: Brief summary of code purpose (max 7 words)

display_title.description: Title for display outputs (charts, images) produced by this code. If omitted, a generic name is used. Use this only when generating visual outputs to provide a more descriptive title for image or chart.

code.description: Python code to execute. Required parameter that contains the Python 3.11 code which will run in the Jupyter Kernel environment.

attachment_urls.description:
List of URLs of user-uploaded files that your code needs to access. Files listed here are transferred into the working directory and become accessible by their original filename. Reference them in code using just the filename, not the full path.

Example 1: attachment_urls=["files/abc123/uploads/2026-03/sales_data.csv"] → in code use: pd.read_csv("sales_data.csv")
Example 2: attachment_urls=["files/abc123/uploads/2026-03/My%20Report.xlsx"] → in code use: pd.read_excel("My Report.xlsx")

data_sample_config.description: Controls pagination and sampling of large text outputs from code execution. Configure this object to adjust how text/plain, markdown and console outputs are displayed. Use for managing large datasets or verbose outputs.

sample_data.description: Controls output sampling behavior. Set to true (default) to return only a portion of large outputs for readability. Set to false to return complete, unsampled output regardless of size.

page.description: Specifies which page of output to display when paginating large results (0-based indexing). Increment this value to view subsequent pages of output.

page_size.description: Defines the number of characters included in each page when paginating. Default is 3000 characters. Adjust based on desired output length and readability.
